subject: Commit right-sizing & renewal uplift scenarios for Acme Data
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie@acme-data.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal and list of questions

Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft renewal. Procurement reviewed the numbers and we have a few asks before we move to legal:

- Can you walk us through the commit tiers? The per-token tiers in the hosted API table look like they assume steady growth; we anticipate a spike in Q4 that may exceed the top tier.
- Is there a cap on renewal uplift year-over-year? We have internal limits for pricing increases and would like to avoid surprise jumps at renewal.
- Can you include an option to right-size the commit at renewal (±20%) without re-pricing?

Attached is our standard vendor questionnaire — we’ll need the pricing table and any exceptions noted for our procurement team.

Sophie Martin
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Data

Attachment: Acme-Vendor-Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@acme-data.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and list of questions

Hi Sophie — thanks, and great questions. High level answers first, details below and I attached a scenario workbook.

1) Commit tiers and overflow: Our hosted API commit tiers are structured to provide per-token discounts once you hit each volume bucket. If you exceed the top committed tier we bill overage at a pre-agreed overage rate (typically 60% of retail). We can also set a soft burst allowance for Q4 if you want predictable costs during the spike.

2) Renewal uplift cap: We can offer a negotiated cap on year-over-year uplift for the contract term. Common asks we’ve granted are 10-12% uplift caps on list rates; I can escalate if Acme needs 5-8%.

3) Right-sizing window: We usually allow a limited right-size at renewal (±15% without reprice). For you I can propose ±20% once per 12-month renewal with a rebaseline if you go beyond that.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send two scenarios (attached workbook): A) conservative growth with a Q4 burst included; B) aggressive growth with a temporary soft-burst and an overage cap.
- If you prefer, we can lock a short-term Q4 burst credit and then re-evaluate at the January cadence.

I’ve cc’d Marissa (AM) and Lauren (Sales Ops) — they can confirm contract-side limits on uplift and approval process.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Renewal-Scenario-3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Acme uplift/commit ask

Team — quick internal note to align before I reply to Sophie:

- Finance has sign-off authority for up to a 12% uplift cap for multi-year renewals; anything below 8% requires only AM + Sales Ops approval.
- We can do a one-time ±20% right-size at renewal as Rafael suggested, but Legal wants the clause to specify it’s one-time and tied to actual trailing 3-month usage.
- For Q4 burst: Sales Ops can configure a 30% soft-burst allowance for one quarter that won’t trigger immediate overage billing; usage beyond that will be billed at the agreed overage rate.

Jordan — if the customer wants a lower overage rate we need a clear replay on expected token distribution (chat vs. embedding) so runtime cost assumptions hold.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Contract-Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Sophie Martin <sophie@acme-data.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Data Procurement <procurement@acme-data.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and list of questions

Thanks for the clarity. A few follow-ups from procurement/finance:

- 12% uplift cap is reasonable, but our CFO wants a hard cap at 10% for the first renewal year if we commit to a 24-month term. Can Redwood do 10% if Acme ups the commit by 15% now?
- For the right-size clause: the ask is that the ±20% is symmetrical and can be executed without a rebaseline (i.e., no repricing) if usage moves down or up within that window. Is the trailing-3-month requirement negotiable?
- For the Q4 burst: instead of a soft-burst allowance, procurement prefers a one-time burst credit that offsets overage charges up to a dollar cap. We’d like the dollar cap to be visible in the contract schedule.

We’ll be on a quick procurement call Friday; can we have a final draft (including the schedule with the dollar cap) by Thursday EOD?

Sophie

Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Summary of what Redwood can commit to for the draft final: 

- Uplift cap: 10% YOY guaranteed for the first renewal if Acme signs a 24-month commitment today and increases committed spend by at least 15% on execution.
- Right-size: one-time ±20% symmetric right-size at renewal with no reprice if the trailing 3-month average is within that window; we’ll make the trailing window optional — if Acme prefers an alternate measurement period we can accept the 6-month average instead.
- Q4 burst: we’ll include a one-time burst credit capped at $45,000 to offset overage charges; the schedule will list the dollar cap and the mechanics.

Action items:
- I’ll send updated SOW/contract language by Thursday EOD with the schedule showing the dollar cap and a clean redline. Lauren — can you confirm we can include the DocuSign link and push to legal for a fast-track review?
- Sophie — if this hits procurement’s needs, we can lock this and route to legal before Friday’s call.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if any of the team wants to walk the scenarios in the attached workbook.

Best,
